doc.what: Close the two gaps the gh #80 re-measure found in readable-content's delivered work: the readability check calls three kinds of unreadable extraction readable, and the Reddit fetcher never fetches the article behind a link post that carries any self-text.
doc.why: Re-measured on cerebro 2026-10-03 for items created since the readable-content deploy (2026-09-30), content under 300 chars: youtube 0/21 (was 56/126), reddit 5/160 (was 270/1594), rss 17/217 (was 154/1720). The RSS share barely moved. 14 of the 17 are Hacker News `Comments` stubs correctly marked title_only (paywalls, PDFs, empty extractions). The other 3 are marked readable and reach analysis as content: trafilatura returned 'This page needs JavaScript.' plus loading text (stoppels.ch), the two glyphs '‹ ›' (frogandtoad.ai), and YouTube's footer navigation (an HN link to youtube.com). `is_readable` in readability.py matches one literal React noscript sentence and only tag-only text, so each new wording of the same failure passes. Separately, 8 of 37 external Reddit link posts since the deploy hold no article text: `_to_content_item` in fetchers/reddit.py appends the post's self-text instead of calling `extract_article` whenever self-text exists, so a link post with a two-line note never gets its article, although trafilatura extracts 23,970 and 13,192 chars from two of those links (ifritnoises.org, binsec.no) today.
decided: The readability check stays shape-based with no bare length floor; one-sentence news blurbs and two-line Reddit questions stay readable (readable-content SC-1).
JavaScript-walled pages are title-only, not rendered (readable-content out of scope).
The fix lives in the one check in readability.py that every consumer already calls; no second check is added.

A Reddit link post to an external article gets the article text alongside the link and any self-text, through the shared `extract_article`; image, video and reddit-internal links stay as they are; a failed extraction keeps today's content.
Items already stored and analysed are not reclassified or re-fetched; a backfill stays a separate, costed decision.
Routing an HN link to youtube.com through the YouTube transcript fetcher stays out of scope (readable-content out of scope: no different route for HN's linked article).
open: How does the check recognize a JavaScript-required notice beyond the one literal React sentence, so wordings like 'This page needs JavaScript.' are caught, without calling an article that discusses JavaScript unreadable?

What shape test replaces the markup-only check so text with no sentence in it at all (site navigation and footer chrome, lone glyphs) is not readable, while a one-sentence blurb and a two-line question stay readable?

impacted.role: `is_readable`, the one check every consumer calls: rejects an anchor-only stub, tag-only text, one literal React noscript sentence (`_JS_WALL_TEXT`), RSS's no-content fallback, Reddit link-only content and YouTube's no-transcript placeholder; everything else is readable
`_to_content_item` builds a link post's content; it appends the post's self-text and only calls `extract_article` when there is no self-text; `refetch_one` reuses `_to_content_item`
`_extract_full_content` returns whatever non-empty text `extract_article` gives and only falls back to the feed entry's own content when extraction returns nothing
skips re-analysing a stored title-only item whose fresh content is still not readable
`get_unreadable_content` selects stored rows by running `is_readable` on their content, for the refetch backfill
`prismis-daemon refetch --type <t> [--dry-run]`: re-extracts rows `is_readable` rejects; still-unreadable rows get `title_only: true` patched with no LLM call, readable ones are re-analysed in place
the readability check's tests: the measured failure shapes, a one-sentence blurb, a two-line Reddit question, article text, content containing a link

constraints.text: No length floor: readability is judged by content shape. Placeholder text is defined once in `readability.py` and imported by the writer.

Content that is not readable (feed stub, JS wall, Reddit `Link: <url>`, "No transcript"/"No content" placeholders, empty) is stored with `analysis.title_only = true`; it stays in the feed, skips deep extraction, and shows a marker in TUI and web.
`_JS_WALL_TEXT` is the single literal 'you need to enable javascript to run this app.', compared against the whole visible text.
The markup-only check rejects only text that is empty once tags are stripped; '‹ ›' and navigation word lists pass.
A link post with any self-text takes the self-text branch and never reaches `extract_article` (line 447).
Any non-empty extraction wins over the feed entry's own content, including junk such as a YouTube footer.

Of 4,853 items fetched in the last 45 days on cerebro that the current check calls readable, a 'has a prose line' test (some line, with tags and URLs removed, holding at least 4 words, each CJK character counting as one word) rejects 31: 20 Hacker News pages of navigation or footer chrome (11 YouTube footers, settings panels, 'Loading', '‹ ›'), 9 Reddit link posts whose content is the link plus one- or two-word comments or a bare markdown link, and 2 Reddit self-posts ('Pls help', 'Tada'). At 3 words it misses the YouTube footer (longest line 'How YouTube works'); at 5 it adds 4 more chrome pages and no real content. Without counting CJK characters it rejects a Japanese news article (no spaces).

In the same 4,853 items, a line naming JavaScript with a requirement verb (enable, disabled, needs, requires, required, turn on) appears in 15 hosts' pages under 1,000 visible chars, every one a wall (Mastodon x12 instances, Notion, nature.com, lemonde.fr, bsky.app, lesswrong.com, developer.apple.com, stoppels.ch, lolchat.rip, 2dwillneverdie.com; longest 381 chars), and in real articles at 1,409, 1,802, 2,670, 4,166, 4,644, 5,858, 6,387 and 23,240 chars (a README's '- No JavaScript required', 'Loading... (JavaScript required)' above a working page, prose about JavaScript). Anubis bot-check pages sit at 1,068.

A rule that drops JavaScript-notice lines and asks whether prose remains, with no size bound, flags no real article but keeps stoppels.ch, lolchat.rip and bsky.app readable, because each has one teaser sentence beside the notice.

The no-length-floor rule exists so genuine short text is never title-only; a size bound applied only to text that already carries a JavaScript notice never touches text without one, so it keeps the rule's purpose, but it is a size threshold the rule's wording does not name.

Once `is_readable` rejects the new shapes, `prismis-daemon refetch --type rss --dry-run` selects the misflagged stored rows with no new code; rows still unreadable are patched title-only without an LLM call.

question: How does the check recognize a JavaScript-required notice beyond the one literal React sentence, so wordings like 'This page needs JavaScript.' are caught, without calling an article that discusses JavaScript unreadable?
answer: Content is a JavaScript wall when a line names JavaScript with a requirement verb (enable, disabled, needs, requires, required, turn on) and its visible text is under 1,200 chars, which on 45 days of cerebro items catches every wall (15 hosts, longest 381 chars, plus Anubis bot checks at 1,068) and no real article (smallest 1,409); boundaries.md:56 is reworded in the same change to say a size bound may only qualify a failure-shape signal and never stands alone, which keeps that rule's purpose of never marking genuine short text title-only.

question: What shape test replaces the markup-only check so text with no sentence in it at all (site navigation and footer chrome, lone glyphs) is not readable, while a one-sentence blurb and a two-line question stay readable?
answer: Content is readable only if some line, with tags and URLs removed, holds at least four words, each CJK character counting as one word: over 4,853 currently-readable cerebro items from the last 45 days this rejects 31, all without prose (20 navigation or footer pages, 9 Reddit link posts holding only the link and one- or two-word comments, 2 two-word self-posts), while three words misses the YouTube footer and five adds only more chrome, and the one-sentence blurb and two-line question fixtures keep their four-plus-word lines.

question: Should an extraction the readability check rejects lose to the fetcher's fallback (the RSS feed entry's own content; for Reddit, today's link-plus-self-text) instead of replacing it, since rss.py takes any non-empty extraction?
answer: Yes: `_extract_full_content` in rss.py uses the extraction only when `is_readable` accepts it and otherwise falls back to the feed entry's own content, and the Reddit link-post path appends the article only when it is readable, which degrades nothing (for Hacker News the fallback is the Comments stub, title-only either way) and keeps a feed's real summary from losing to page chrome.

doc.purpose: Pages that delivered no content (a JavaScript wall in any wording, site navigation or footer text, lone glyphs) are recognized as title-only by the shape they share rather than by one literal string each, and a Reddit link post gets its article even when the poster wrote a note, so analysis runs on real content or is honestly labeled title-only.
doc.form:
Two general shape rules in the one check, and two fetchers that stop preferring junk.

1. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/readability.py` `is_readable` (line 82) keeps its placeholder checks (RSS's no-content fallback, Reddit link-only content, YouTube's no-transcript content) and the constants and `format_*` helpers the fetchers import. It replaces three narrow checks with two general ones. (a) The has-prose rule replaces the markup-only check and the anchor-only check: content is readable only if some line, after tags and URLs are removed, holds at least four words, with each CJK character (kana and CJK ideographs) counting as one word. The HN `Comments` anchor stub (one word once its tag is stripped), tag-only text, '‹ ›' and navigation lists all fail it. (b) The JavaScript-wall rule replaces the `_JS_WALL_TEXT` literal: content is a wall when a line names JavaScript with a requirement verb (enable, enabled, disable, disabled, need, needs, require, requires, required, turn on) and its visible text is under 1,200 characters. The constant carries a one-line comment naming its measurement (cerebro, 2026-10-03: walls up to 1,068 chars, real articles from 1,409). Both rules are pure functions over the content string, with no length floor on text that lacks a JavaScript notice.

2. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/fetchers/rss.py` `_extract_full_content` (line 249) returns the extraction only when `is_readable` accepts it, and otherwise returns `_fallback_content(entry)` as it already does when extraction returns nothing.

3. `daemon/src/prismis_daemon/fetchers/reddit.py` `_to_content_item` (line 440): for a link post whose URL is neither an image nor a reddit page, and not already stored readably, it calls `extract_article` whether or not the post has self-text, and builds `format_reddit_link_only(url)`, then the self-text if any, then the article text when `is_readable` accepts it. Text posts, image, video and reddit-internal links, and the already-readable skip behave as today. `refetch_one` gets this through `_to_content_item` unchanged.

4. `docs/architecture/boundaries.md` line 56 becomes: no length floor on its own; readability is judged by content shape, and a size bound may only qualify a failure-shape signal (the JavaScript-wall rule), never stand alone.

5. Tests in `daemon/tests/unit/test_readability_unit.py`: not readable for the stoppels.ch extraction, '‹ ›', the YouTube footer list, the Mastodon and Notion notices, nature.com's notice, and the existing failure fixtures; readable for the existing one-sentence blurb and two-line question, a Japanese news paragraph with no spaces, a 1,500-char article containing 'Loading... (JavaScript required)', a README line '- No JavaScript required' inside a long document, and content that merely contains a link. Fetcher tests serve pages from a local HTTP server (no live third-party URL): RSS falls back to the entry summary when the page extracts to navigation text and keeps a readable extraction; a Reddit link post with self-text gets the article appended, and a failed or unreadable extraction leaves link plus self-text. Each new test is shown red with its rule removed.
commitments: One check, `is_readable` in readability.py, still decides readability for every consumer; no second check is added.
Text with no line of at least four words (tags and URLs removed, CJK characters counted one each) is not readable.
A JavaScript-requirement line makes content a wall only when its visible text is under 1,200 characters; text without such a line is never judged by its size.
A fetcher never prefers an extraction the check rejects over its own fallback.
A Reddit link post to an external article gets the article text whether or not the poster wrote self-text.
boundaries.md line 56 states the no-length-floor rule with its one permitted qualifier.
sacrifices: Reddit self-posts with no line of four words ('Pls help', 'Tada') become title-only; their title carries all there is.
A JavaScript wall longer than 1,200 visible characters stays readable; none was seen in 45 days of cerebro items.
Items already stored and analysed keep their classification until `prismis-daemon refetch` is run for them, a separate costed step.
An HN link to youtube.com is still extracted as a page and becomes title-only rather than getting the video's transcript.
Reddit link posts with self-text now cost one article fetch each per new post.
doc.risk: If the has-prose rule rejects a real short format not seen in the 45-day sample (a list of short items with no four-word line), those items become title-only and skip deep extraction until the rule is widened; if a real article under 1,200 characters carries a JavaScript-requirement line, it is labeled title-only.

scrutiny.test: T0 purpose: docs/IDEA.md:39 makes prismis a structured data source agents query; boundaries.md:55 promises unreadable content is stored title-only so its summary is not presented as real analysis. Recognizing failure shapes by what they share closes the wordings the literal check missed (stoppels.ch, frogandtoad.ai, 11 YouTube footers, 12 Mastodon walls, Notion, nature.com and others measured on cerebro).
scrutiny.failureCase: The change were neutral on what reaches analysis as content.

scrutiny.test: T1 owners: boundaries.md:55 lists JS walls and empty content as not readable, which both rules implement; boundaries.md:56 (no length floor, judged by shape) is kept for every text without a JavaScript notice and reworded in the same change to name its one qualifier; readable-content SC-1's fixtures (one-sentence blurb, two-line question, article with a link) each hold a line of four or more words and stay readable.
scrutiny.failureCase: A contract required a literal-only check or forbade any size term at all.

scrutiny.test: T2/T6 evidence on the same noun: both thresholds were measured on the stored content the check actually runs on (4,853 currently-readable cerebro items over 45 days), not on fixtures: the prose rule rejects 31 items, every one without prose; the JavaScript rule under 1,200 chars catches 15 wall hosts plus Anubis (1,068) and no article (smallest 1,409). The three named misses were reproduced through `extract_article` and `is_readable` on 2026-10-03.
scrutiny.failureCase: A threshold were chosen from a fixture the test built.

scrutiny.test: T3 degrades: two two-word Reddit self-posts become title-only (title carries all there is); walls over 1,200 chars stay readable (none observed); one more article fetch per Reddit link post with self-text.
scrutiny.failureCase: A real short item with prose were reclassified title-only.

scrutiny.test: T4 reuse: extends `is_readable` in place (readability.py:82), `_fallback_content` in rss.py, `extract_article` and `format_reddit_link_only` in reddit.py; the refetch backfill picks up newly-recognized stored rows with no new code.
scrutiny.failureCase: A second readability check or a second extractor were added.

scrutiny.test: T5 real-system proof: after deploy, `prismis-daemon refetch --type rss --dry-run` on cerebro reports the newly-recognized stored rows, and the per-source short and title-only counts for items created after deploy are re-measured against the 2026-10-03 numbers.
scrutiny.failureCase: The only proof were unit fixtures.

scrutiny.test: T7 consumers of `is_readable`, enumerated with `grep -rn 'is_readable(' daemon/src`: analysis.py:84 (title_only), orchestrator.py:423 (skip re-analysing still-unreadable), storage.py:748 (refetch selection), refetch.py:226; plus the two new fetcher calls. Callers of `extract_article` (`grep -rn 'extract_article(' daemon/src`): rss.py, reddit.py and refetch.py, whose RSS path already discards an unreadable extraction and leaves stored content alone.
scrutiny.failureCase: A caller kept preferring an unreadable extraction over existing content.

scrutiny.test: T8 shape: both rules are structural properties of the text (a prose line exists; a requirement notice in a small page), replacing three literal matches whose next miss was a new wording.
scrutiny.failureCase: The fix added more literal strings.

scrutiny.test: T9 six months: wall pages that grow past 1,200 chars or use a verb outside the list stay readable (fails toward today's behavior); the constant carries its measurement date so a re-measure has a baseline.
scrutiny.failureCase: A drift made the rule mislabel real content silently.

scrutiny.test: T10 undo: revert the commit; stored rows are reclassified only by an operator-run refetch, which can be rerun.
scrutiny.failureCase: The change rewrote stored data on deploy.

scrutiny.test: T11 class: the class is 'a failure page recognized by one literal'; swept the currently-readable corpus for other gate shapes (bot checks, captcha, Cloudflare, cookie and subscribe walls, 403/404, too many requests) under 3,000 chars: only Anubis bot checks, which carry a JavaScript notice and fall under the wall rule; and 'a fetcher preferring junk over its fallback' swept across every `extract_article` caller.
scrutiny.failureCase: A sibling failure shape or a third junk-preferring fetcher stayed unhandled.
